findings.title: The stronger no-late-publication claim misses the consuming continuation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited robustness/cleanup issue; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: One fixed date and the public zero-entropy phrase. The wallet callback schedules abort with two nested queueMicrotask calls and returns matched:true.
findings.expected: Under the strengthened askWallet/addendum promise, reject with the signal reason and publish no late match.
findings.observed: The run resolved with an aborted signal; onMatch ran once and observed that signal already aborted.
findings.impact: A host can receive a late recovery after stopping. SearchRun retains its weaker next-turn contract, so this is a limited inconsistency in the strengthened remediation claim rather than a demonstrated breach of the original contract. The native checker was not shown to produce a wrong wallet or leak a secret.
findings.recommendedFix: Check the signal in the caller immediately before result publication and final return, including after helper awaits. Keep the shared wallet-answer validator.
findings.requiredVerification: Zero onMatch calls, rejection with the same abort reason, and normal matched true/false controls for every search path.

findings.title: A split returns shares and original text from different input revisions
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve supported asynchronous result ownership before release.
findings.reproduction: Gate createShares, start splitBackup for public phrase A in direct mode, change request.mnemonic to the valid public phrase B, then release the gate.
findings.expected: Return the original normalized phrase captured for this split, or reject a stale request.
findings.observed: held is phrase A and original is phrase B in the same successful BackupSplit. The real SSKR platform and split verification were used.
findings.impact: A browser/library host that edits its request during asynchronous WASM readiness can pair an unrelated displayed original with the actual backup. Immutable native CLI input is not affected by the demonstrated schedule.
findings.recommendedFix: Capture the normalized original and all operation inputs before awaiting, and build the result exclusively from that snapshot.
findings.requiredVerification: A gated ordinary-object edit must never mix revisions; keep both direct and Seedshift behavior and entropy cleanup.

findings.title: Saved QR sidecars bypass the staging-copy warning handler
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited robustness/cleanup issue; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Fail only removal of .mnemocode-export-* after QR publication. Rendering/QR encoding return public opaque bytes; publication is real. Exercise both QR helpers and the real runEncode card-qr route.
findings.expected: The saved sidecar counts as saved, a warning identifies the remaining private staging copy, and the command completes without retrying the published result.
findings.observed: Both document and sidecar were present and complete, but runEncode rejected with LeftStagingCopy. Both QR helpers also rejected, with zero cleanup warnings through terminalNotice. Two common-save controls passed; all three sidecar cases failed.
findings.impact: The command reports an error after successful publication; a share-sidecar loop can stop before later files. The exception still names the private copy, so this is not a hidden-copy or file-content-loss claim.
findings.recommendedFix: Route sidecar publication through writeSaved while retaining the selected path and the warning. Do not suppress ordinary save failures.
findings.requiredVerification: Both sidecar helpers, Encode, and SSKR sidecar loops complete with exactly one warning per leftover; EEXIST and genuine failed writes still fail.

findings.title: Unknown prototype-named options print inherited object values
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited robustness/cleanup issue; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Call optionLabel for __proto__, constructor and toString; run the actual built CLI table --word abandon --__proto__ with a public value.
findings.expected: A string naming the typed unknown option, with the command refused.
findings.observed: The helper returned an object or function. The real CLI refused correctly but printed '[object Object] setting'. Known and ordinary unknown labels were correct.
findings.impact: Broken refusal text and a declared string-return contract. The parser fix is working; no prototype pollution or bypass of unknown-option refusal is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use Object.hasOwn for label lookup or a null-prototype map, then retain the existing fallback.
findings.requiredVerification: Exact string labels and exact unknown/repeated/missing-value refusals for inherited names, with normal-label controls.

findings.title: Transport readers abandon internal share-byte arrays without wiping
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited robustness/cleanup issue; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Retain references to Uint8Array.from allocations while reading one published deterministic share. Also repair CRC32 after setting a reserved metadata bit, then exercise the intended metadata refusal.
findings.expected: Internal decoded arrays are wiped when their local job ends; a successfully returned caller-owned urToTransport array remains usable.
findings.observed: Nonzero internal arrays remained after readShare (1), Share.read (2), bytewordsToUr (1), and an Invalid SSKR share metadata refusal (1). The caller-owned-result control passed.
findings.impact: Best-effort cleanup is missing for transient typed arrays. No heap dump, secret theft, or guaranteed whole-memory-erasure claim; immutable share strings already have documented JavaScript limits.
findings.recommendedFix: Add try/finally wiping for discarded transports and wipe allocations on rejection, without wiping a transport returned to its caller.
findings.requiredVerification: Capture ended internal buffers on successful parsing and intended refusal, and preserve the caller-owned successful output.

findings.title: An exported share-format mirror still returns undefined for unknown forms
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited robustness/cleanup issue; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Call shareFormatMirroring with typo, null and 5; compare all five supported encoded forms.
findings.expected: Refuse an unsupported format before returning a ShareFormat.
findings.observed: All three invalid inputs returned undefined; all five supported controls passed. Share.write's original reproduction is now fixed.

informationalReview.title: Executable host getters are read again after validation
informationalReview.assessment: Informational robustness scope: changing kind getters selected NoProtection and real MNCL bytes; changing matched getters counted one match after validating boolean false. These require executable host objects, cannot come from JSON or typed native CLI input, and are not a security claim against a dishonest host. Ordinary original reproductions remain fixed. Snapshot validated fields or explicitly document stable-input assumptions.

informationalReview.title: Checked checksum resamples a getter-backed input
informationalReview.assessment: An index getter returning 0 during validation and 1 later was read twice and produced false. This proves resampling, not invalid-index acceptance or incorrect checksum math. Copy once and validate/compute the same owned list, or state a stable-input precondition.

informationalReview.title: The historical cleanup probe has a narrower oracle than the adjudicated contract
informationalReview.assessment: Its overwrite-after-preflight case passed. Its old expect(failure).toBeUndefined still fails on LeftStagingCopy, while the two stronger new controls verify complete publication plus a warning and a real retained copy. Preserve that historical failure; do not make it green by hiding the copy.

informationalReview.title: aud-014-staging.test.ts is meaningful but covers only the common save path
informationalReview.assessment: All three tests passed. They assert a typed cleanup outcome, saved bytes, a warning, ordinary silent success, and EEXIST refusal. Two audit controls additionally assert the retained document, exact staging path, warning kind, returned path and one write. They do not cover QR sidecars or prove every save goes through writeSaved.

informationalReview.title: Descriptor chunks and MACs have cleanup by source
informationalReview.assessment: readBoundedDescriptor registers each chunk before readSync and wipes in finally; digestFits wipes the owned MAC in finally. Existing new UTF-8 tests observe returned buffers, not all descriptor chunks. Partial-read-then-throw allocation-capture tests would improve coverage without large input.

recommendations.title: Optional encapsulation hardening for PivotBasis
recommendations.change: add returns its stored object. Its type is readonly and current callers do not mutate it. Freezing or returning a copy is optional runtime hardening, not a reproduced solver defect.
